findings.reason: the bound cannot mean both "prioritise beyond this" and "stop calling it queued beyond this"; the plan must split the constants or state which reading a past-bound entry gets, or §5's measure is unsatisfiable for the long-wait case §3 exists to protect.
findings.text: §3 makes REVIEW_QUEUED_BOUND_SECONDS the queue's starvation threshold ("an entry that has waited longer … is admitted ahead of every entry that has not") and tells §5's obligations reading to use "that same constant", but the obligations view reads that age the other way: `_queued_review_fields` returns None once `age > REVIEW_QUEUED_BOUND_SECONDS` (`obligations.py:305`), so a run that has waited past the bound is the queue's top priority for admission yet stops being read as queued — the exact surface §5's done-when asserts will report it as queued

findings.reason: the builder must name the real post-queue phase (the launched pointer's own phase, e.g. `starting`/`working`) for this step to be written so it can fail.
findings.text: §4's last done-when requires the coordinator's follower to see the run "move from queued to dispatched", but the plan defines only the `queued` phase and no target-phase word, and the live-pointer vocabulary has no `dispatched`: the pre-spawn phases are `{starting, launching, launcher, dispatching}` (`recovery.py:6431`) and the follower's states are `SETTLED_STATES` (`ticker.py:329`), so the assertion names no value a test can check
